prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1227; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Claimant reports stopping at a red light when the insured vehicle made contact with the rear bumper. Claimant states she is experiencing right knee pain and stiffness. Police report requested. No attorney representation noted; claimant is handling communications directly.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. She reports the knee pain worsened overnight and she has an appointment with her primary care provider this week. Explained the medical documentation we will need to evaluate the injury claim, including treatment records and any imaging. Claimant asked general questions about the process and is comfortable proceeding without representation.

Entry 3: Insured's statement obtained. Insured acknowledges following too closely and did not see the stopped vehicle until impact. Insured reports no injuries. Photos of both vehicles received, showing rear damage to claimant's vehicle and front damage to insured's vehicle. Scene diagram reviewed against police report.

Entry 4: Received initial treatment records from claimant's provider. Diagnosis indicates a sprain of the right knee with swelling. Physical therapy referral noted. Recommended follow-up in four weeks. Claimant has not yet submitted any repair estimate or bills for the vehicle beyond the initial shop assessment.

Entry 5: Liability assessment completed. Based on the insured's admission and the physical evidence, liability appears clear. Advised claimant of the next steps, including the property damage settlement process and how medical bills will be reviewed once received. Claimant acknowledged the explanation. File remains open pending completion of treatment and receipt of final bills.
